solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Carrier's very French sound

indicators.note: the word sound tells us to say a French word aloud and enter the English word it resembles

parts.note: très is the French word for very

explanation.surface: Someone praising a delivery firm's distinctly Gallic tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noun in the surface but signals a homophone of the French très.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat board with a rim is a carrier for food or drinks.

clue.text: With transport and currency, I must move to get grip

indicators.note: must move tells us the letter I is shifted to another place within the assembled letters

parts.note: trains are a form of transport
FX is short for foreign exchange, that is, currency

explanation.surface: Instructions for a traveller sorting out transport and money before taking hold of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must move' shifts the I of the assembled letters from its place after the A to sit just before the last letter; FX is the dealers' shorthand for foreign exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone motionless with fascination or horror is to grip them.

clue.text: Everyone on university vessel washed up

parts.note: all means everyone
a vial is a small glass vessel

explanation.surface: Everyone at a university's boat finished, as if the ship ran aground.
explanation.definitionFit: Deposited by flowing water, as silt and sand are washed up by rivers.

clue.text: Women's crew with fewer pounds? None at all

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
a rowing eight is the crew of a racing boat
less means fewer

explanation.surface: A rowing club's women's eight, slimmer than before, has shed every last pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a little scene: if you have no pounds of mass at all, you weigh nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no mass registering on the scales at all, as astronauts float in orbit.

clue.text: Rule for new mischievous young swimmer

indicators.note: for here means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: elven means elfin, impish and mischievous

explanation.surface: A rule change aimed at an impish young swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rule for new' tells us to put R for N in ELVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eel is a juvenile fish, a young swimmer.

clue.text: Continental city generating in a suitable manner

parts.note: a German is from continental Europe
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A European city producing things appropriately.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevantly or pertinently, done in a fitting or appropriate way.

clue.text: Eccentric poets make hay, squandering second disposable income

indicators.note: eccentric tells us the letters of the following words are rearranged
squandering means throwing away, so a letter is dropped from the words

explanation.surface: Odd poets wasting time while the sun shines.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S (second) from POETS MAKE HAY and rearrange the remaining eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings left after tax and deductions, the income available to spend.

clue.text: In high places bring back whiskey that is special

indicators.note: bring back means the word for whiskey is read in reverse

parts.note: rye is a type of whiskey
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Up in the mountains, someone orders a special whiskey to be brought back.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagles' nests on crags, and by extension any lofty dwelling or vantage point.

clue.text: Where to investigate former wife?

parts.note: suss out means investigate
an ex is a former spouse

explanation.surface: Asking where to dig into an ex-wife's past.
explanation.walkthrough: SUSS is British slang for working something out; the definition 'Where' is answered by a place, an English county on the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: An English county on the south coast is a place, an answer to where.

clue.text: Rod's American guitar starts to lose excitement

parts.note: axe is slang for a guitar, spelt AX in American English

indicators.note: starts to refers to the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Rod, a musician, finds his US-made guitar no longer thrills him.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod looks like a man's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft or spindle about which a wheel turns is a metal rod.

clue.text: Rovers' kits right back used as women's clothing

indicators.note: back tells us the letter for right is shifted further back within the phrase

explanation.surface: A football club's team strip being worn as ladies' fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ROVERSKITS and move its leading R back to sit between the I and the T. 'right back' looks like a defender's position.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer skirts worn over another skirt or petticoat are garments for women.

clue.text: One who delivers various changes

indicators.note: changes tells us to rearrange the letters of the preceding word

explanation.surface: A courier whose deliveries keep altering.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer is one who delivers people from danger, as in deliver us from evil.

clue.text: Left brave struggling in dodgy canoe to capsize

indicators.note: in tells us one group of letters is placed inside another
dodgy means unsound, so the letters of the boat are rearranged
struggling tells us the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A brave paddler fighting in a leaky canoe that is about to tip over.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams nest: 'struggling' makes VERBAL, and 'dodgy' makes OANCE, which is split after its O to hold it. 'Left' looks like the past tense of leave but is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose balance and fall over, as a boat does when it tips.

clue.text: Find success in a letter to First Lady

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
Eve was the first woman, according to Genesis

explanation.surface: Someone striking it lucky by writing to the President's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests the US President's wife, but here it is the first woman in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To accomplish or attain a goal is to find success.

clue.text: King's declaration unexpectedly made Ava heir

indicators.note: unexpectedly tells us the following words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch surprisingly names someone called Ava as successor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' suggests a monarch, but it is Martin Luther King, whose 1963 speech bears this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther King's famous civil-rights speech of 1963 is known by this phrase.

clue.text: Eye could be faulty, losing a bit of focus for a little time

indicators.note: losing, with for, means one letter is dropped and another takes its place

parts.note: defective means faulty

indicators.note: a bit of means the first letter of focus

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An optician's diagnosis of a defective eye that briefly loses focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye' is a private eye. In DEFECTIVE, F (a bit of focus) is replaced by T.
explanation.definitionFit: A private eye is slang for a private investigator.

clue.text: Genealogical science for the lady's almost entirely uninteresting

parts.note: her means belonging to the lady

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: all means entirely
dry means dull or uninteresting

explanation.surface: A woman finding family-tree research nearly completely boring.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of coats of arms and family descent, tied to genealogy.

clue.text: Strong red pigment in volcanic orifice

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a vent is an opening in a volcano
heme, the American spelling of haem, is the red pigment of blood

explanation.surface: A powerful red colouring found in a volcano's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceful, passionate or intense, as in a vehement protest.

clue.text: As graduate your field of study is underwater equipment

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
thy is the archaic form of your
a sphere is a field of activity or study

explanation.surface: Telling a new graduate their subject is the kit for diving.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel diving sphere lowered on a cable was used for deep-sea observation.

clue.text: Spoils the outskirts of Hackney, like Slough?

parts.note: mars means spoils

indicators.note: the outskirts of means the outer letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Is east London's fringe ruined in the manner of Slough?
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, often mocked, but here it is a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or bog, so boggy, waterlogged ground fits.

clue.text: Wild beasts tied down by many a lassie

indicators.note: tied down by means held within the following words

explanation.surface: Untamed animals restrained by lots of girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyalas are African antelopes, wild animals of southern Africa.

clue.text: Irregular content of racy clichés

indicators.note: content of means the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A critique of the uneven substance of risqué stock phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: Not cyclic, not following a repeated pattern, hence irregular.

clue.text: Decay rate can be changed by this, note

definitions.text: Decay rate can be changed by this, note

indicators.note: can be changed tells us the letters of the opening words are rearranged

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A dentist suggesting that tooth decay rates can be altered by some measure.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DECAY RATE are the answer plus TE; the whole clue hints that supervising children's habits can change how fast their teeth decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Supervised care of young children during the working day, where diet and brushing can be watched.

clue.text: What Adam did before Eve died receiving a bit of love

indicators.note: before places the letter for died ahead of the rest
receiving means the name takes another letter inside it
a bit of means the first letter of love

explanation.surface: Biblical tale: Adam's deed came before Eve died, with a touch of love.
explanation.walkthrough: From the rhyme 'When Adam delved and Eve span, who was then the gentleman?': Adam dug the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam dug the ground in the old rhyme, and to dig is the old sense.

clue.text: Having no children, bestow identity on couple from Lyon with much magnificence

parts.note: SP stands for sine prole, Latin for without issue, used in genealogies
lend means bestow, as in lend dignity
ID is short for identity

indicators.note: a couple from means the first two letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A childless French pair given a new identity in grand style.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (sine prole) is a genealogical abbreviation meaning without children.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something gloriously or magnificently, in grand fashion.

clue.text: Cutter increases noise

indicators.note: noise tells us a word heard spoken gives the entry

parts.note: adds means increases

explanation.surface: A cutting machine that gets louder as it works.
explanation.definitionFit: An axe-like tool with an arched blade at right angles, used for shaping timber.

clue.text: Eery events disturbed today's vigil

indicators.note: disturbed tells us the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Spooky happenings unsettled the watch kept overnight.
explanation.walkthrough: The vigil is the eve, so today's eve is the evening just gone, last night.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for the evening of the previous day; a vigil is the eve of a feast.

clue.text: Return plaything to European island

indicators.note: to means the reversed toy is attached onto the letter for European
return means the word for plaything is read backwards

parts.note: a toy is a plaything

explanation.surface: Sending a toy back to a European island.
explanation.walkthrough: An eyot is a small island in a river, such as those in the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A small river islet, also spelt ait, is a kind of island.
